title: 2025-04-11-admin-telemetry-snapshot-and-archival-options-with-aurora-medics
summary: High-level review of admin telemetry: what events Redwood captures by default, export/stream options (S3, webhooks, SIEM connectors), retention controls, encryption/KMS handling for exported archives, and implications for Aurora Medics' SOC2/ISO controls and data residency requirements. Agreed to run a 1-week export POC and share security pack + sample schema.
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack + export schema by 2025-04-14
Aurora to provision S3 test bucket and share access by 2025-04-18
Run 1-week export POC (logs + admin events) starting 2025-04-21
Schedule follow-up to review POC results week of 2025-04-28
action_items: Maya Chen: Send Redwood security pack, SOC2 snapshot, and export field schema — due 2025-04-14
Jorge Morales: Create S3 bucket + IAM role for POC and share ARN — due 2025-04-18
Ethan Park: Provide sample webhook connector config and small script for parsing — due 2025-04-15
Samir Kapoor: Share Aurora's retention policy and legal hold contacts — due 2025-04-16
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-11
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz, Samir Kapoor, Jorge Morales (Aurora Medics)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everybody, thanks for taking the time. quick intro — I'm Maya, I'm the AE on the account, and Ethan is our solutions engineer. today we want to focus on admin telemetry, what we capture by default and the export/archival options for compliance. Samir, thanks for lining this up.
[00:18] Samir: Thanks Maya. yes big focus for us is SOC two and ISO audit readiness, but also data residency and being able to show provable admin trails for any privileged activity.
[00:28] Ethan: Great. i'll kick off with what Redwood captures out of the box — and i'll try not to make this too dry — high level we capture authentication events (logins, SSO/SAML assertions, token creations), RBAC changes (role grants, policy edits), API key issuance/rotation, model deployment actions, console actions (user CRUD on teams/projects) and system-level alerts like failed calls or escalated errors.
[00:48] Dr. Lena: Quick clarification — when you say "model deployment actions" do you also include who triggered a rollback or change in model config? we need that audit trail.
[00:55] Ethan: Yes, we capture actor, timestamp, IP, the request path, and a minimal request payload summary — not the full prompt content by default — so you get a delta of config changes (e.g., flags, image/model id). sometimes the transcriber will show that as "model config delta" in the logs.
[01:12] Jorge: Do you capture session ids or KV cache hints? I've seen other systems leak cache keys that are sensitive.
[01:18] Ethan: We capture a session id and request id for correlation. we do not log KV cache contents; that's never persisted in audit logs. occasionally in older exports there was a field labeled "K-V cash" in the CSV because of transcription mis-translation but that's not actual cached content.
[01:34] Samir: Good to hear. on retention — what options do we have? our policy is 7 years for admin trails for regulated devices.
[01:41] Maya: Out of box retention on hosted Redwood Console is 90 days for detailed logs and 365 days for summary-level events. for enterprise customers we offer configurable retention via Dedicated or Private — you can set raw retention to whatever you need if you route exports to your archive.
[02:00] Samir: So does that mean we need Dedicated or Private to meet 7 years?
[02:04] Ethan: Not necessarily. you can use hosted + continuous export to an Aurora-owned S3 bucket and retain long-term there. the key is export granularity and encryption. exports can be full event JSONs or compressed summaries.
[02:18] Maya: i'll add that many customers use lifecycle rules on S3 to move to Glacier or equivalent. Redwood supports daily batched exports and near-real-time streaming via webhooks or Kafka connectors to SIEMs.
[02:33] Dr. Lena: For the PII angle — if an event contains user identifiers, does Redwood redact or pseudonymize before export?
[02:40] Ethan: By default event payloads include user ids and role names. we have an option for pseudonymization prior to export (hashing user ids) or field-level redaction. that's a per-customer config for the export job. if you need automatic redaction we can enable it in the pipeline. note there may be tradeoffs for correlation during incident response.
[03:02] Jorge: Can we get an example schema? we'll need to map fields into our SIEM for alerting.
[03:08] Maya: absolutely — we'll send a sample schema (json lines) that shows fields like event_type, actor_email, actor_id, actor_ip, request_id, timestamp, resource_type, change_set, export_version.
[03:20] Samir: How do you handle encryption of exported archives and keys? Aurora mandates KMS-managed keys with rotation and key access logging.
[03:27] Ethan: For S3 exports we can encrypt with customer-managed KMS keys (CMKs) in your account; Redwood will write to the bucket using an IAM role you create. for streams to external SIEMs we support TLS mutual auth; payloads are encrypted in transit. for hosted archival we can also store encrypted with Redwood-managed keys but for compliance we recommend customer-managed keys.
[03:48] Dr. Lena: If we use Redwood-managed KMS, do you provide access to the audit trail of key usage?
[03:54] Ethan: Redwood can provide key usage logs but Redwood-managed keys won't show inside your cloud KMS console. that's why many customers prefer to give us a write-only role to their bucket so KMS logs live in their account.
[04:06] Maya: also worth calling out: we keep an immutable event sequence number so you can prove ordering in case of legal hold.
[04:14] Samir: about exports — formats and sizes. do you gzip daily dumps? what's the schema versioning story if Redwood changes fields?
[04:23] Ethan: Exports are ndjson by default, compressed with gzip. we include a header file with export_version and schema_version. when fields change we bump schema and publish a changelog; we support back-compat by tagging old exports with their version.
[04:36] Jorge: any SIEM connectors out of the box? Splunk? Datadog?
[04:40] Maya: We have community and enterprise connectors: Splunk HEC, Datadog logs intake, Sumo Logic, and AWS Kinesis. or you can use a webhook to a SIEM ingestion endpoint.
[04:52] Samir: on SSO and RBAC — if someone authenticates via SAML from our IdP, do you connect to our SAML assertion so we can prove MFA was enforced?
[05:00] Ethan: We record the SAML assertion result (accepted/failed) and include assertion id and auth_methods. we don't persist the full SAML assertion unless you opt in. MFA presence is recorded in the event metadata (e.g., auth_method: saml+mfa).
[05:15] Dr. Lena: For org admins making console changes, is there a way to require dual control (two approvers) and have that reflected in the audit logs?
[05:22] Ethan: Redwood console supports approval workflows in Dedicated and Private deployments; the audit log records the approver ids, timestamps, and the approval token. hosted customers can use a webhook approval flow with your internal approver service.
[05:34] Maya: quick note — a few customers have used our webhook stream to push events into an internal "approval gate" before the change commits; that requires low-latency policy but it's doable.
[05:45] Jorge: Do audit exports include full request/response bodies for admin API calls? sometimes we need that detail for forensics.
[05:51] Ethan: By default we include request metadata and a summarized response status and error codes. full bodies are considered sensitive and are only included if you opt into high-fidelity logging; that is gated behind a privacy config and increases storage and cost.
[06:05] Samir: Are there rate limits or cost implications for exporting every event in near real-time?
[06:11] Maya: There's a throughput tier for streaming. hosted includes a baseline free streaming quota, beyond that there's usage-based pricing. Dedicated customers can configure higher throughput with burst capacity.
[06:22] Dr. Lena: Data residency question — if we need logs stored in eu only, can exports be region-locked?
[06:28] Ethan: Yes. exports to your buckets in eu regions are supported. for hosted retention in-region we can pin where data is stored, or Private deployment in your VPC ensures everything stays in-country.
[06:40] Jorge: How are deletions handled? for example if a user's account is deleted do their past admin actions remain?
[06:45] Ethan: Audit events are immutable by design. account deletions do not remove historical audit events. we support pseudonymization for GDPR workflows but keep an immutable record showing that an action occurred (e.g., actor hashed).
[06:58] Samir: Legal hold and eDiscovery — can we trigger a hold to prevent lifecycle rules from deleting exports?
[07:04] Maya: Yes, if you keep exports in your S3 you control lifecycle. if Redwood hosts your archive we have a legal hold mechanism where we mark exports as "hold" preventing purge; that can be coordinated with our support ops.
[07:17] Jorge: For the POC — what will you stream? full admin events or a subset?
[07:22] Ethan: For the 1-week POC we'll stream admin events (role changes, key rotations, model deployments, SSO auth events). we'll keep prompts and model input excluded.
[07:31] Dr. Lena: We also want an example export that shows timestamps in UTC and includes the actor IP and CIDR if available.
[07:37] Maya: noted — schema will include utc_timestamp, actor_ip, actor_cidr if resolvable, request_id.
[07:44] Samir: About indexing in our SIEM — can you include a static mapping file for field to SIEM index names?
[07:50] Ethan: Yes, we'll include a recommended mapping for Splunk/Datadog. also the sample parsing script.
[07:58] Maya: couple quick compliance questions from our side — do you have any internal requirements for the S3 role we need?
[08:02] Jorge: we usually want a write-only role that can put objects and put-object-tagging, and a lifecycle policy granting listing only to our audit service.
[08:10] Ethan: that's exactly what we recommend — and we'll give a CloudFormation snippet for the role.
[08:15] (crosstalk)
[08:20] Samir: One more — do you provide attestations for log completeness? like a signed digest?
[08:25] Ethan: We provide a monotonically increasing sequence id and hashes of daily export batches. some customers integrate that into their WORM storage and store the digest in an external ledger for tamper evidence.
[08:38] Dr. Lena: Any gotchas around timezones, clock skew? we need consistent timestamps for audits.
[08:43] Ethan: All events are normalized to UTC at ingestion and we include both customer-local timestamp if provided and the ingestion timestamp. we also log the server offset to help with skew analysis.
[08:55] Maya: ok let's summarize next steps quickly: we send the security pack and schema, Ethan will provide sample webhook and CFN snippet, Aurora provisions bucket and role, run 1-week POC, then reconvene.
[09:10] Samir: sounds good. thanks all.
[09:13] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with links.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts observed (e.g., "K-V cash" appears in one auto-label). Customer emphasized long-term retention and KMS-managed keys.
